input: Learn to play chess openings from YouTube tutorials

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Chess openings is a vast topic — knowing whether they want a broad survey of many openings or deep mastery of one or two shapes the entire learning path.
Current skill level (complete beginner, casual player, club-level) determines which openings and YouTube channels are appropriate — beginner-friendly content vs. advanced theory.
Some players prefer aggressive, tactical openings (e.g. King's Gambit) while others prefer solid, positional ones (e.g. London System) — this filters which tutorials to watch.
The amount of time available per day/week directly determines how ambitious the plan can be and how to pace the learning schedule.
Whether they play online (Chess.com, Lichess) or over-the-board affects which openings are practical and how they will apply what they learn.
Knowing which color(s) they want to learn openings for (White, Black, or both) defines the exact set of tutorials needed — they are entirely different repertoires.
Understanding what 'done well' means — memorising move sequences, understanding the ideas, or winning more games — determines how to structure practice alongside watching.

gold.taskTitle: Learn chess openings via YouTube tutorials
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to study and practice chess openings by watching YouTube tutorials.

questions.title: How many openings do you want to learn right now?
questions.description: Should the plan cover one or two specific openings in depth, or a broader survey of several openings across different responses?

questions.title: What is your current chess experience level?
questions.description: Are you a complete beginner, a casual player who knows the rules, or someone with club/tournament experience? This determines the complexity of tutorials to target.

questions.title: Do you prefer aggressive or solid, positional play?
questions.description: Your style preference (e.g. tactical gambits vs. quiet strategic setups) will filter which openings and YouTube channels best match you.

questions.title: How much time per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Knowing your available study time — e.g. 30 minutes a day vs. a few hours on weekends — shapes how ambitious and paced the learning plan should be.

questions.title: Where do you mainly play your chess games?
questions.description: Do you play online on platforms like Chess.com or Lichess, or over the board at a club or with friends? This affects which openings are most practical to learn.

questions.title: Which color or colors do you want openings for?
questions.description: Do you want to learn openings for White, Black, or both? White and Black repertoires are entirely separate and require different tutorials.

questions.title: What does successfully learning an opening mean to you?
questions.description: Is the goal to memorise the first several moves, deeply understand the strategic ideas, or directly see improvement in your game results?
